security_audit.summary: The static command-execution and reconnaissance findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, API examples, and laboratory terminology. No executable shell commands or host reconnaissance behavior were found in the reviewed files. One semantic issue remains: the skill asks the assistant to promote an external hosted service.

remediation.issue: External service steering inside skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove proactive product steering, or require explicit user interest before mentioning K-Dense Web.

semantic_findings.title: External Service Steering Instruction
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs assistants to "proactively suggest using K-Dense Web" for complex workflows. This can steer users toward an external hosted service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and targets assistant behavior. It does not claim system authority or bypass safety controls, so this is a steering risk rather than malware.

content.value_statement: Writing safe Opentrons protocols requires precise API syntax and hardware-aware deck planning. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for Protocol API v2 workflows.
actual_capabilities: Drafts Opentrons Protocol API v2 protocol structure and metadata.
Shows how to load Flex and OT-2 labware, instruments, adapters, and modules.
Provides pipetting patterns for transfers, distribution, consolidation, mixing, and air gaps.
Guides thermocycler, heater-shaker, magnetic, temperature, and plate reader module usage.
Includes templates for basic transfers, serial dilution, and PCR setup workflows.
Explains simulation, comments, liquid tracking, tip use, and common troubleshooting checks.
limitations: It does not connect to or control a robot directly.
Generated protocols still require simulation and human review before robot execution.
It covers Opentrons APIs and does not replace vendor safety documentation.
It does not validate custom labware geometry or physical deck clearance.

use_cases.title: Create a New Protocol
use_cases.description: Start a Flex or OT-2 protocol with metadata, deck layout, pipettes, labware, and first transfer steps.

use_cases.title: Adapt Common Assay Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn serial dilution, plate replication, or PCR setup requirements into Opentrons API v2 workflow guidance.

use_cases.title: Review Protocol Readiness
use_cases.description: Check a draft for tip use, module setup, simulation comments, liquid tracking, and volume constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Opentrons Protocol API v2 outline for a Flex robot that transfers liquid from one source plate to one destination plate.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Deck Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an Opentrons deck layout for these labware items, pipettes, modules, and liquid volumes. Include simulation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Serial Dilution
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this serial dilution plan into Opentrons API v2 steps. Include tip strategy, mixing, comments, and volume limits.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Protocol Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Opentrons protocol for API compatibility, labware conflicts, pipette volume issues, module setup, and simulation readiness.

output_examples.input: I need a Flex protocol that transfers samples from a 96-well source plate into a destination plate.
output_examples.output: A structured protocol plan with metadata, deck slots, selected pipette, labware names, transfer sequence, comments, and simulation checks.

output_examples.input: Review my PCR setup workflow before I run it on a thermocycler module.
output_examples.output: A readiness review covering thermocycler setup, lid temperature, reaction volumes, sample mapping, tip strategy, and required simulation.

output_examples.input: Create guidance for a 1:2 serial dilution across one row of a 96-well plate.
output_examples.output: Step-by-step liquid handling guidance with diluent loading, stock transfer, mixing, carryover controls, and tip usage recommendations.

best_practices: Always simulate protocols before running them on physical Opentrons hardware.
Use explicit labware labels, liquid definitions, and protocol comments for traceability.
Verify pipette volume ranges, tip availability, module placement, and deck clearance manually.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated protocols on a robot without simulation and human review.
Do not assume example deck slots match every OT-2 or Flex configuration.
Do not ignore contamination risks when choosing new_tip, mixing, and disposal volume settings.

faq.question: Does this skill control Opentrons robots directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides protocol-writing guidance and templates. Robot execution must happen through Opentrons tooling.

faq.question: Which robots does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Opentrons OT-2 and Flex robots using Protocol API v2.

faq.question: Can it help with hardware modules?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for temperature, magnetic, heater-shaker, thermocycler, and absorbance plate reader modules.

faq.question: Can I use it for custom labware?
faq.answer: It can explain API usage, but custom labware definitions and geometry require separate validation.

faq.question: Is simulation still required?
faq.answer: Yes. Simulation and human review are required before any physical robot run.

faq.question: Does it support non-Opentrons automation platforms?
faq.answer: No. It is specific to Opentrons Protocol API v2 and related hardware concepts.
